title: Classical Music And Classroom Management https://smartclassroommanagement.com/2009/08/27/classical-music-and-classroom-management/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin makes the case that classical music, already known to enhance certain cognitive abilities, can also function as a subtle classroom management tool by lowering tension and building positive associations with learning. He cites the stress-reducing effect of classical music on heart patients (comparable to Valium) and a 2004 London Underground initiative that reportedly reduced vandalism, assault, and robbery in targeted stations by playing classical music, alongside commercial examples like hotels and retailers using music to shape customer mood. He recommends specific composers (Mozart, Bach, Tchaikovsky, Vivaldi) while cautioning against jarring or overly dramatic pieces like Wagner, and stresses that the practice must be consistent, played daily as part of a set morning routine rather than used occasionally, in order to build a lasting association between the music and calm, focused behavior.
points: Classical music can reduce tension and build positive learning associations, functioning as a subtle, low-effort classroom management tool.
Real-world evidence (a London Underground initiative, hospital stress studies) supports music's calming and behavior-shaping effects in other contexts.
Consistency matters: the music must play daily as part of a fixed morning routine to build a durable association, not be used sporadically.
Composer choice matters — smooth, non-jarring works (Mozart, Bach, Vivaldi) are recommended over pieces with sudden crescendos, like Wagner.
quotes: Having classical music playing in the background when students enter the classroom can reduce tension and anxiety, making them less inclined to act up. It also builds a subconscious association between the sound of the music and behavior that is conducive to learning.
A study on heart patients found classical music to have the same stress reducing benefits as the drug Valium.

In 2004, classical music was piped into London Underground train stations and into certain dangerous neighborhoods. As a result, incidences of vandalism, assault, and robberies dropped in those areas by as much as 37%.

The very act of walking into certain classrooms can trigger feelings of restlessness in students. Think of a Walmart store on the day after Thanksgiving. Chaotic situations cause people to behave poorly and do things they wouldn’t normally do.
But it’s not something you do just once in a while. It must be done every day in conjunction with a specific morning routine.
Never let your students forget that your classroom is a place for learning. Besides having a potent calming effect, classical music is a perfect reminder.
